abstract: Telomeres safeguard chromosome-end integrity, yet population-scale dissection of telomere-length genetics has been largely restricted to humans. Here, we report a 3.01-Gb telomere-to-telomere (T2T) genome of Holstein cattle that resolves repeat-rich chromosome ends and centromeres and enables telomere-length quantification at single-chromosome-end resolution. Holstein chromosome ends show marked telomere-length asymmetry and end-specific variation in telomere variant repeats, subtelomeric tandem repeats, GC/CpG composition, and DNA methylation. Using sequencing-depth-corrected telomere-length phenotypes from 9,591 cows, teloGWAS identifies major loci encompassing RTEL1, CTC1, and TERT, while multi-tissue eQTL, sQTL, TWAS, and co-expression analyses prioritize CTC1 and implicate DNA replication, DNA repair, and stress-response networks. Together, these findings extend population-scale telomere genetics beyond humans and establish a sequence-resolved framework for chromosome-end biology and telomere-informed livestock genomics.
